source.title: Product Appearance Inspection Common Defect Classification and Acceptance Criteria
source.organization: Shenzhen Xinyinhai Electronics Co Ltd Dongguan Branch
source.filename: 鑫银海产品外观检验标准_英文翻译.docx

purpose: To give operators and inspectors a comprehensive understanding of the company’s product appearance inspection standards and requirements, enable sound acceptance decisions, reduce component losses, and ensure that the quality of products manufactured by the company meets customer requirements.
scope: Applicable to all products manufactured by the company and all externally purchased parts and components.

conditions.label: Lighting
conditions.detail: Illumination: Normal fluorescent lighting, with indoor illuminance of at least 300 lx.

conditions.label: Viewing distance
conditions.detail: Viewing distance: Inspect by looking directly at the product from a distance of 30 cm.

conditions.label: Observation time
conditions.detail: Observation time: Inspect each surface for 3–5 seconds.

surfaces.definition: A surface directly visible under normal conditions of use.
A surface not directly visible under normal conditions of use.
An internal product surface that is not visible during normal visual observation.

severity.name: Critical defect
severity.definition: A defect that poses a risk to personal safety or may harm human health, such as sharp points, sharp edges, small parts or unsanitary conditions.

severity.name: Major defect
severity.definition: An appearance defect that may make the product unsalable and is highly likely to cause consumer or distributor complaints or returns. Examples include short shots on the exterior of a product, fingerprints that cannot be wiped off the product surface, illegible printed content, and severe scratches.

severity.name: Minor defect
severity.definition: A minor appearance defect that does not directly affect product sales; that is, a defect other than a CR or MA defect. Examples include slight oil stains, scuffs, weld lines and sink marks.

criteria.text: Not acceptable.
Not acceptable.
Not acceptable.

defects.name: Drag whitening
defects.description: Streak-like marks, generally on the sidewalls of a product, that resemble scratches and are accompanied by whitening.

criteria.text: Not acceptable.
Acceptable when limited to spots, haze or faint streaks that are not visible from 30 cm. Pronounced streaks that are visible from 30 cm are not acceptable.
Acceptable.

additional: Slight drag whitening, appearing only as spots or haze, can be concealed by spray painting and need not be screened out before spray painting.

images.alt: A pink oval marks small white drag marks along the lower edge of a red molded surface.
images.caption: Spot-like drag whitening

images.alt: Two green circles mark spot-like and hazy whitening on a red molded edge.
images.caption: Spot-like and hazy drag whitening

defects.name: Dirt, oil stains and fingerprints
defects.description: Spots, shiny oily marks, or marks left by contact with fingers.

criteria.text: Acceptable when the affected area is small, can be wiped clean easily, and is not visible from 30 cm. A large affected area that is difficult to wipe clean and is visible from 30 cm is not acceptable.

Acceptable when the affected area is small, can be wiped clean easily, and is visible only at an angle that catches reflected light. A large affected area that is difficult to wipe clean is not acceptable.
Acceptable, except for customers with special requirements.

images.alt: A red circle marks dark dirt spots beside a switch on a yellow plastic housing.
images.caption: Dirt

images.alt: A pink circle marks a dark oily mark on a blue plastic hinge area.
images.caption: Oil stain

images.alt: An orange circle marks a faint fingerprint on a glossy purple plastic surface.
images.caption: Fingerprint

defects.name: Flash, sharp points and burrs
defects.description: Excess material in the form of thin fins, cone-shaped projections or strands on a component surface or edge.

criteria.text: Not acceptable if it protrudes above the product surface and can be felt by hand.
Not acceptable if it protrudes above the product surface and can be felt by hand.
Acceptable provided that it does not interfere with assembly or generate loose foreign material.

images.alt: A red oval marks a thin fin of excess plastic across an opening in a purple molded part.
images.caption: Flash

images.alt: A red circle marks a small pointed projection on a turquoise surface.
images.caption: Sharp point

images.alt: A red oval marks excess material along the curved edge of a purple plastic part.
images.caption: Burr

defects.name: Surface step mismatch
defects.description: A step caused by a mismatch at a parting surface between two mold inserts or between the cavity and core halves due to machining tolerances, or by misalignment during ultrasonic welding.

criteria.text: Acceptable if the step is ≤ 0.25 mm and no sharp edge or sharp corner can be felt by hand.
Acceptable if the step is ≤ 0.25 mm and no sharp edge or sharp corner can be felt by hand.
Acceptable.

images.alt: A red oval marks a surface step along the side joint of a yellow plastic housing.
images.caption: Surface step mismatch

defects.name: Weld lines
defects.description: Visible linear marks that generally cannot be felt as a raised or recessed area. They usually occur on parts with complex geometry or around through-hole features. Also known as knit lines or melt-joining lines.

criteria.text: Acceptable if visible only at an angle that catches reflected light, or if consistent with the customer reference sample.
Acceptable.
Acceptable.

additional: In general, slight weld lines can be concealed by spray painting and need not be screened out.

images.alt: A pink oval marks a thin weld line across a green molded surface, labelled Class A in the source.
images.caption: Class A surface weld line

images.alt: A pink oval marks a faint diagonal weld line on a turquoise surface, labelled Class B in the source.
images.caption: Class B surface weld line

defects.name: Sink marks
defects.description: Depressions or pits, generally occurring at thick walls or reinforcing ribs.

criteria.text: Acceptable if not visible from 30 cm. Not acceptable if visible from 30 cm, or assess against the customer reference sample.
Assess against the established acceptance limit or the customer reference sample.
Acceptable.

additional: Slight sink marks that do not affect spray painting or label application need not be screened out before those operations. Sink marks that affect screen printing, pad printing or label application are not acceptable.

images.alt: A pink circle marks a depression near the hinge of a blue plastic product, labelled a severe sink mark.
images.caption: Severe sink mark

images.alt: A pink circle marks a shallow sink mark on the raised edge of a yellow molded housing.
images.caption: Slight sink mark

defects.name: Short shots
defects.description: Insufficient plastic material resulting in an incomplete part.

criteria.text: Not acceptable.
Not acceptable.
Assess according to whether functionality, strength, assembly or appearance is affected.

images.alt: Pink circles mark incomplete yellow molded posts in the source example of a short shot affecting assembly.
images.caption: Short shot affecting assembly

images.alt: A red oval marks a missing notch of material at the lower edge of a black key marked 4.
images.caption: Severe adverse effect on appearance

images.alt: A pink oval marks missing plastic beside a white mounting hole in the source example affecting assembly and safety.
images.caption: Short shot affecting assembly and safety

defects.name: Gas marks
defects.description: Areas on the product surface that differ in color or luster from the surrounding areas.

criteria.text: Assess against the customer reference sample.
Assess against the customer reference sample.
Acceptable.

additional: Need not be screened out on parts intended for spray painting.

images.alt: A red oval marks a pale irregular patch on a green plastic strip, labelled a gas mark.
images.caption: Gas mark

defects.name: Gaps
defects.description: A gap resulting from interference between internal parts during assembly.

criteria.text: Acceptable if the gap is ≤ 0.25 mm and internal components are not visible. Intentionally designed cosmetic grooves are excluded.
Acceptable if the gap is ≤ 0.25 mm and internal components are not visible. Intentionally designed cosmetic grooves are excluded.
Acceptable.

images.alt: A black oval marks the gap along the joint between two pink housing parts.
images.caption: Gap between assembled parts

defects.name: Scratches and impact damage
defects.description: Marks that are perceptible as raised or recessed areas, or marks that are not perceptible to the touch but show obvious whitening that differs from the component color. The marks are visually apparent.

criteria.text: One scratch that is not perceptible to the touch is acceptable if its length is ≤ 5 mm and its width is ≤ 0.1 mm. Two such scratches are acceptable if spaced 30 mm apart. A scratch that is perceptible to the touch and visible from any angle is not acceptable.

One scratch that is not perceptible to the touch is acceptable if its length is ≤ 10 mm and its width is ≤ 0.25 mm. Two such scratches are acceptable if spaced 30 mm apart. A scratch that is perceptible to the touch and visible from any angle is not acceptable.
Acceptable.

additional: Scratches with a raised or recessed profile cannot be concealed by spray painting and must be screened out before spray painting. Whitening from scratches with no raised or recessed profile can be concealed by spray painting and need not be screened out before spray painting.

images.alt: A pink oval marks a narrow white scratch on green plastic, identified in the source as perceptible to the touch.
images.caption: Scratch perceptible to the touch

images.alt: A pink oval marks a faint scratch on red plastic, identified in the source as not perceptible to the touch.
images.caption: Scratch not perceptible to the touch

defects.name: Off-color specks and color contamination
defects.description: Specks or patches on the material surface whose color differs from the product color.

criteria.text: One speck with a diameter of ≤ 0.3 mm is acceptable. Color contamination is acceptable if it is not visible from 30 cm; otherwise, it is not acceptable.

Two specks are acceptable if each has a diameter of < 0.5 mm and the distance between them is > 50 mm. Color contamination is acceptable if it is not visible from 30 cm; otherwise, it is not acceptable.
Acceptable.

additional: Reject transparent parts with these defects. These defects need not be screened out on parts intended for spray painting.

images.alt: A pink circle marks one black speck on yellow plastic; the source annotation states 0.3 mm or smaller.
images.caption: Black speck ≤ 0.3 mm

images.alt: Red circles mark black specks on yellow plastic; the source annotation states larger than 0.5 mm.
images.caption: Black specks > 0.5 mm

images.alt: A red oval marks a faint off-color patch on a light-colored textured plastic surface.
images.caption: Color contamination

defects.name: Deformation
defects.description: Twisting, inward depression, outward bowing or insufficient flatness.

criteria.text:
Assess according to the overall assembly result. Any deformation that adversely affects assembly, functionality or safety is not acceptable.

Slight deformation is acceptable if it has little effect on appearance and can be corrected by securing the deformed area with screws.

images.alt: A pink rectangle marks one distorted white key in a row, identified as affecting functionality.
images.caption: Deformation affecting functionality

images.alt: A row of molded white keys bows noticeably; the source identifies severe deformation affecting assembly and functionality.
images.caption: Severe deformation affecting assembly and functionality

images.alt: A row of molded white keys shows slight bowing, identified in the source as not affecting functionality or appearance.
images.caption: Slight deformation with no effect on functionality or appearance

defects.name: Ejector and pressure whitening
defects.description: White spots or rings on the front surface opposite an ejector pin, or whitening caused by an uneven assembly fixture or excessive pressure.

criteria.text: Acceptable if the whitening is not visible from 30 cm and there is no obvious bulge on the component surface; otherwise, it is not acceptable.
Acceptable if the whitening is not visible from 30 cm and there is no obvious bulge on the component surface; otherwise, it is not acceptable.
Acceptable if there are no obvious cracks at corners or feature bases and product functionality, strength and assembly are not affected; otherwise, it is not acceptable.

additional: On parts intended for spray painting, this defect need not be screened out if there is no obvious surface bulge and there are no cracks at corners or feature bases.

images.caption: Whitening at an ejector pin location

images.caption: Whitening caused by assembly fixture pressure
